Who's going to train them for three years?" Justice Arora said that she had heard that some law firms in India had stopped hiring A0 associates, even as concerns grow over the potential impact of AI on employment opportunities for young lawyers. items.title: The case for fast-tracking reforms in India to recognise emergency arbitration in statute
items.summary: Recognition of emergency arbitration in India's Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 requires a straightforward legislative amendment consistent with already established case law and international precedent which would demonstrate India's continued commitment to becoming a leading hub for international arbitration. As two years have passed since the Ministry of Justice published the Arbitration and Conciliation (Amendment) Bill 2024 for public comment, we make the case for prioritising enactment of the parts of the draft that relate to emergency arbitration, to signal India's commitment to driving the uptake of international arbitration. The Amendment Bill The stated purposes of India's Arbitration Amendment Bill are threefold: strengthen dispute resolution, reduce court interventions in arbitration and ensure the timely conclusion of arbitration proceedings. Development of the law to recognise and facilitate emergency arbitration assists with achieving all three of those goals: it helps to afford expeditious interim relief to parties awaiting constitution of an arbitral tribunal, which in turn decongests civil courts. items.title: Supreme Court Justice Joymalya Bagchi bats for dedicated AI courts to decide mutual consent divorce cases
items.summary: Supreme Court judge Justice Joymalya Bagchi on Saturday proposed the establishment of round-the-clock artificial intelligence (AI) courts to deal with mutual consent divorce cases, saying routine judicial work should be shifted away from human judges. Justice Bagchi was speaking at the Just Tech National Conclave organised by Dharmashastra National Law University at Jabalpur on the role of AI and technology in the administration of justice. " We should, in my understanding, hive off the mutual divorce cases and have 24/7 AI divorce courts so that there will be ease of access to justice and no wastage of valuable human resources on completely non-adjudicatory exercises, " he said. Justice Joymalya Bagchi Hive off the mutual divorce cases and have 24/7 AI divorce courts. Justice Bagchi said the judiciary's mounting pendency necessitates technological intervention and use of AI tools. "We are sitting on a pile of over five crore cases. And with the given infrastructure and human resources, we are not going to go anywhere near delivering quick, efficient and timely justice until and unless we have transformative interventions through artificial intelligence tool deployments," he said.

items.title: The right to protest in the age of surveillance: Can dissent remain free under the digital gaze?
items.summary: A democracy is tested not merely by the freedoms it grants its citizens, but by the extent to which it allows them to exercise those freedoms without fear. The right to protest is among the most visible expressions of a constitutional democracy. Yet, in an age where technology can identify, track and digitally profile individuals with unprecedented precision, the very act of exercising this right may expose citizens to a different form of State scrutiny. On November 3, 2026, a petition before the Supreme Court challenged the use of CCTV cameras and facial recognition technology by the State to monitor, identify and track individuals participating in public protests. The Supreme Court issued notice on the petition , bringing into focus the constitutional question of whether participation in a public protest can justify State surveillance and the processing of individuals' personal data. Historical evolution of the right to protest in India At Independence, India inherited a colonial administrative and policing structure in which public assemblies and political demonstrations were frequently subjected to executive control. items.title: Women in high public office does not mean equality has been achieved: Justice BV Nagarathna at Oxford
items.summary: Supreme Court Justice BV Nagarathna recently said that the presence of women in high public offices does not mean equality has been achieved across the society. She added that even a guaranteed right can be difficult to exercise in practice due to cost, delay and social consequences. "The existence of women in high public office does not establish that equality has been achieved throughout society. A woman may hold a senior position while other women remain excluded from education, employment, property, or effective legal remedies," the judge said. The judge made the comment while delivering the inaugural Cornelia Sorabji Memorial Lecture at the Oxford India Centre for Sustainable Development in Somerville College, University of Oxford, on November 18. The lecture was on the topic "The Doors She Opened: Cornelia Sorabji and the Progress of Women's Rights in India." In a rejoinder filed on November 21, NWMI said paragraphs of the affidavit “read like a catalogue of admissions” and that terms such as “mistaken identity”, “verification” and “merely removed” and “released upon identification” are euphemisms “deployed to soften the description of actual restraint”. items.summary: Padmaja Venugopal, daughter of former Kerala chief minister and Congress veteran K Karunakaran, has apologised to Congress workers for joining the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in 2024. The apology comes amid growing opposition within the Congress to her proposed return to the party following her exit from the BJP on November 19. In a Facebook post on Saturday, November 21, Padmaja said she had realised that her decision to join the BJP had deeply hurt Congress workers who were fond of both her and her father. She said she was preparing to return after recognising the impact her departure had on the party and its workers. “When I said, while resigning, that joining the BJP was a wrong decision I had made in an emotional moment, I was speaking from my heart. I realised that the decision I had taken back then deeply hurt many Congress workers who loved both K Karunakaran and me. It was this realisation that prompted me to prepare for a return,” she said. Stating that she was not aspiring for any position within the party, Padmaja said her only wish was to become a Congress worker again.
